chapter: The Living World and Biological Classification
trick: The taxonomic hierarchy narrows as you go down, and the mnemonic King Philip Came Over For Good Soup gives you Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species. As you descend, the number of organisms falls and the shared characters rise.

video.query: the living world taxonomy five kingdom classification class 11 biology

data.prompt: Arrange the taxonomic categories from the widest to the narrowest.

items.label: Kingdom
items.note: The broadest group, such as Animalia

items.label: Phylum
items.note: Chordata, for animals with a notochord

items.label: Genus
items.note: Homo — the first word of the scientific name

items.label: Species
items.note: sapiens — the narrowest group, and the second word of the name

trick: Follow two questions down the plant kingdom: does it have vascular tissue, and does it make seeds? Algae have neither, bryophytes neither, pteridophytes have vessels but no seeds, gymnosperms have naked seeds, angiosperms have seeds inside a fruit.

video.query: plant kingdom algae bryophytes pteridophytes gymnosperms class 11 biology

data.prompt: Which group does each plant or feature belong to?

items.label: The amphibians of the plant kingdom; need water for fertilisation
First plants with proper vascular tissue but still no seeds
Seeds are naked, not enclosed in a fruit
Seeds enclosed in a fruit; double fertilisation occurs

trick: Classify by body plan, not by looks. Symmetry, body cavity and segmentation decide the phylum, which is why a starfish and a jellyfish sit far apart despite both living in the sea, and why a whale is grouped with a bat.

video.query: animal kingdom classification phyla porifera arthropoda class 11 biology

data.prompt: Match each phylum with an example and its key feature.

pairs.right: Sponges; body with pores, no true tissues
Jellyfish and Hydra; stinging cells and radial symmetry
Tapeworm; flat, bilaterally symmetrical, no body cavity
Earthworm; segmented body with a true coelom
Insects; jointed legs and a chitin exoskeleton, the largest phylum
Starfish; spiny skin and a water vascular system

trick: The flower is four whorls from the outside in: sepals, petals, stamens, carpels. Green protection first, colourful attraction next, then male, then female. Learn the order once and any flower diagram labels itself.

trick: There are only four animal tissue types, and every organ is built from them: epithelial covers, connective supports and joins, muscular contracts, nervous conducts. Ask what the tissue is doing and its type names itself.

video.query: animal tissues epithelial connective muscular nervous class 11 biology

data.prompt: True or false? Mark each statement about animal tissues.

items.why: It has cells suspended in a fluid matrix, plasma, which is exactly the connective tissue plan. This surprises most students.

items.statement: Epithelial tissue always has a free surface.
items.why: One side faces a cavity or the outside and the other rests on a basement membrane, which is why it lines and covers.

items.statement: Cardiac muscle is under voluntary control.
items.why: Cardiac muscle is involuntary, though it is striated like skeletal muscle. It is the one striated muscle you cannot command.

items.statement: Neurons can divide to replace themselves easily.
items.why: Most mature neurons lose the ability to divide, which is why nerve damage heals so poorly.

items.statement: Tendons join muscle to bone and ligaments join bone to bone.
items.why: Both are dense connective tissue, and mixing the two up is the classic slip.

trick: Learn the organelles by their job, not their shape. Mitochondrion the power house, ribosome the protein factory, lysosome the suicide bag, Golgi the packaging and dispatch department. The nickname is usually what the question is really asking for.

video.query: cell the unit of life organelles structure and functions class 11 biology

data.prompt: Match each organelle with what it does.

pairs.right: Releases energy as ATP; the power house of the cell
Builds proteins; found free or on rough ER
Carries out photosynthesis; only in plant cells
Holds the DNA and controls the cell's activity

trick: Identify a biomolecule by its building block. Amino acids make proteins, monosaccharides make carbohydrates, nucleotides make nucleic acids, fatty acids and glycerol make fats. Name the monomer and you have named the family.

video.query: biomolecules carbohydrates proteins lipids nucleic acids enzymes class 11

data.prompt: Which class of biomolecule does each belong to?

items.label: Made of amino acids joined by peptide bonds
Made of glycerol and fatty acids
Cholesterol and the cell membrane's phospholipids
Built from nucleotides, each a sugar, a phosphate and a base

trick: Meiosis is two divisions but only one round of DNA copying, which is exactly why the chromosome number halves. Mitosis copies once and divides once, so the number stays. Count copies against divisions and the two can never be confused.

video.query: cell cycle mitosis meiosis phases class 11 biology

data.prompt: One of these is not a stage of mitosis. Which, and why?
data.because: The other four are the four stages of mitosis in order. Pachytene belongs to prophase I of meiosis, where it is the substage in which crossing over takes place. Its five substages — leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene and diakinesis — exist only in meiosis, because only meiosis has to pair homologous chromosomes.
